name: self-evolve
description: The self-improvement loop: nightly runs (defects first, at most one focused verified change), a night-drained autonomous backlog, a same-day repair loop, and a measured fitness landscape with noise-aware selection over time (kept / regressed / confounded — fix-forward, never auto-revert).

jobs.name: self-evolve-repair-tick
jobs.description: Scan terminal failures (dead event deliveries, failing scheduled jobs, abandoned runs), dedupe them into repair requests, reclaim stale repair turns, and start at most one repair turn

jobs.name: self-evolve-backlog-tick
jobs.description: Night shift for the backlog: reclaim stale in-flight items and, inside the drain window under the per-night cap, start the oldest open autonomous item at low agent-queue priority so operational work always goes first

jobs.name: self-evolve-metrics-tick
jobs.description: Sample the fitness landscape — reliability, friction, workload regime, the LLM latency probe, stalled queues — into selfevolve_metrics; the trends are what the loop evolves against

jobs.name: self-evolve-outcome-tick
jobs.description: Selection over time: judge changes older than outcome_measure_days against the metric they declared (noise-aware, confounder-gated), and watch the guardrail metrics across the window

jobs.name: self-evolve-nightly
jobs.prompt: First GET /api/self-evolve/settings (token in env); if enabled is false, do nothing else — end this run. Then run the self-evolve skill: read the skill at .qwen/skills/self-evolve/SKILL.md and follow it exactly. Work its steps in order. Step 0 — state: GET /api/self-evolve/backlog?status=open and GET /api/self-evolve/runs?limit=5 so you do not re-raise or redo what is already tracked; reset any in-flight backlog row older than the inflight_stale_hours setting (GET /api/self-evolve/settings, default 12) via POST /api/self-evolve/backlog/{id}/reset; reclaim any run row stuck 'running' for over 2 hours via POST /api/self-evolve/runs/{id}/finish with an error. Step 1 — start a run (POST /api/self-evolve/runs, trigger schedule). Step 2 — the defect pass (defects beat novelty): GET /health (load errors), GET /api/catalog (apps with load errors), GET /api/events/health (stuck deliveries), the jobs_failing metric, GET /api/self-evolve/repair/requests (terminal failures are already watched by the repair loop — do not duplicate work it has a repair request for, and do not re-open a failure it classified expected for its recorded reason), the queues_stalled metric in GET /api/self-evolve/metrics/latest (a queue holding work with no progress is a defect even though its job reports success), and re-verify the last 5 runs' changes still work. Step 3 — the learning pass (bounded): if a news digest app is installed read the last 7 digests (at most one candidate from news, only if it maps onto something this system already does), plus one web search rotating by weekday (Mon agent frameworks, Tue FastAPI/async patterns, Wed databases/migrations, Thu LLM-agent patterns, Fri task automation, Sat dashboard/frontend patterns, Sun security) — one search, at most 2 results. Step 4 — the usage pass: the state of the data the platform holds for the user — for each collection the catalog lists: total, last-30-day growth, the newest 10 through the app's own list endpoint, and the question 'could the user tell at a glance what each item is and is for?'; a shape that costs them is an improvement candidate whose evidence is the observation itself, never a pre-written idea — derive the improvement, do not re-raise anything already in the open backlog. Step 5 — the architecture pass (a bounded scan, not a rewrite): duplicated concepts across mini-apps and the frontend — the same logic in two places, an endpoint reimplementing another endpoint or an SDK helper, a mini-app privately owning what should be a shared capability, convention drift within one app — unify, split, refactor or propose a shared concept; backend AND frontend in scope. Step 6 — selection with the trash test (the value sentence must name which side it helps: the system, or the user's life and business), and AT MOST ONE focused change, ROOT-CAUSE ONLY — a workaround is never an end state; if the root fix is bigger than the run's budget, file it to the backlog with tier=autonomous and the plan in why so the night drain builds it — verified end-to-end before the run is recorded. Note the division of labour: open tier=autonomous backlog items are worked by the night drain (POST /api/self-evolve/backlog/tick, one item per turn, low priority, until the drain cutoff hour) — do NOT implement backlog items yourself during the run; your one discretionary change is for fresh findings, and you may still dismiss a backlog item you find stale or wrong. Also: 'regressed' change outcomes (GET /api/self-evolve/metrics/outcomes?verdict=regressed) are top-priority defects — FIX FORWARD, never revert: diagnose why the change moved its metric the wrong way (read the change, read the metric samples) and ship a NEW root-cause change that corrects the regression, verified, with its own expected_metrics. Never auto-revert a commit — later work, including features the user requested, may stand on it; a revert only ever happens on the user's explicit instruction, recorded in the run, and is then recorded via POST /api/self-evolve/metrics/outcomes/{id}/reverted. After ANY change you made, commit your change to the agent's git repository — the commit message must end in provenance: run=<run_id> (find a change later with git log --grep 'run=<run_id>') — and pass the short SHA as genome_commit; in the finish payload declare expected_metrics (name, direction, baseline from GET /api/self-evolve/metrics/latest read BEFORE the change) for any change expected to move a metric. Mine recent completed agent turns for friction the user experienced — a correction, a re-ask, a rejected suggestion, or them doing by hand what the system should do — logging each via POST /api/self-evolve/friction that GET /api/self-evolve/friction shows is not already there (the interactive agent logs friction in the moment; this is the backstop for what it missed). The autonomy line is non-negotiable: anything touching only the platform itself (code, database, internal APIs, screens, platform ops, migrations, new shared concepts, new mini-apps) is decided and implemented autonomously — the agent knows better on architecture and functionality, and a plan ends in implementation, not a request for permission; anything reaching the user's world (sending in their name or to third parties, acting for them, spending, deleting their data, publishing, credentials, the vault, data/, changes to how the user is messaged) is never autonomous — file it tier=proposal with a firm recommendation; a genuine security hole is fixed now and reported. The loop is the DECIDER on its own backlog (the user's Adopt/Dismiss buttons stay as override, but no item waits on them): on this run every OPEN backlog item gets a decision — adopt it via POST /api/self-evolve/backlog/{id}/adopt (platform-internal, the trash test still holds; the night drain builds it), dismiss it via POST /api/self-evolve/backlog/{id}/dismiss (evidence stale or wrong, reason recorded), or keep it a proposal strictly because it reaches the user's world; a proposal with no reply after 7 days is decided by the loop (world-reaching: prepare — draft, stage, schedule — never the outward act of send, spend, delete or publish, which stays the user's explicit go). Record the run via POST /api/self-evolve/runs/{id}/finish with what you found and what you changed. Send a message via POST /api/self-evolve/notify if and only if you made a change or have a concrete proposal — a run with nothing to say sends nothing.
jobs.description: Nightly self-improvement: defects first, then learning, at most one focused verified root-cause change — or nothing

jobs.name: self-evolve-meta
jobs.prompt: First GET /api/self-evolve/settings (token in env); if enabled is false, do nothing else — end this run. Then the weekly META run of the self-evolve loop — the loop reviewing itself. First read the 'Meta-run (weekly)' section of .qwen/skills/self-evolve/SKILL.md and follow it exactly. In short: start a run (POST /api/self-evolve/runs, trigger 'schedule'); review the fitness landscape (GET /api/self-evolve/metrics/latest?hours=168, GET /api/self-evolve/fitness?hours=168) and the loop's own track record (GET /api/self-evolve/runs?limit=14, /api/self-evolve/backlog, /api/self-evolve/repair/requests, /api/self-evolve/metrics/outcomes, /api/self-evolve/friction?limit=100). Then the meta pass: (0) backlog decisions — resolve any open proposal past its 7-day deadline per the Triage decider rule in the skill (world-reaching: prepare, never the outward act); (1) friction mining — a cluster of the same kind (3+ in 7 days) becomes a hypothesis through the trash test, tiered per the autonomy line; (2) procedure review — only with strong evidence that the loop's OWN procedure is the bottleneck, revise the skill text or loop settings (higher evidence bar than a normal run; platform-internal only, root cause only); (3) at most ONE meta change, verified end-to-end, committed to the agent's git repository (the commit message must end in provenance: run=<run_id>). The autonomy line and every guardrail in the skill apply unchanged. Notify only when there is something to say.
jobs.description: Weekly meta-run: the loop reviews its own fitness and track record; friction becomes hypotheses; the procedure itself can evolve (higher evidence bar)

views.title: Backlog
views.description: What the loop found but did not do. The loop is the decider on this list: it adopts, builds and dismisses on its own runs — Adopt and Dismiss are your override, not the decision path. Dismissing records the reason so the idea is never re-proposed.
views.empty: No open ideas. Entries only survive the trash test: real evidence, clear value, no trash.

actions.label: Adopt
actions.confirm: Start implementing this now? It runs through the agent queue and may take several minutes.

actions.label: Dismiss
actions.confirm: Dismiss this idea? It will not be re-proposed.
actions.promptHint: Why dismiss this idea? (recorded, so it is never re-proposed)

views.title: Change outcomes
views.description: Selection over time: each change declares the metric it should move; after a few days the measured delta decides, gated on the workload. If the workload regime moved, the verdict is 'confounded' — not blamed on the change — and is re-judged once it settles. Regressed changes are fixed forward, never auto-reverted.
views.empty: No declared outcomes yet — runs that make a change declare which metric it should move.

views.title: Friction log
views.description: Logged moments where you had to step in — a correction, a re-ask, a manual fallback. The loop's highest-density signal: recurring friction is what new capabilities grow from.
views.empty: No friction logged yet — every one of these is a signal the loop can act on.

views.title: Fitness landscape
views.description: What 'better' means, measured — sampled every 30 minutes. Every metric here is lower-is-better; '24h ago' shows the trend.
views.empty: No samples yet — the first lands within 30 minutes (System → Jobs: self-evolve-metrics-tick).

views.title: Runs
views.description: One row per run. An empty Changed column on a healthy run is the expected state — the loop is allowed to do nothing.
views.empty: No runs yet — the first fires tonight at 02:00 (System → Jobs: self-evolve-nightly).

views.title: Repairs
views.description: Terminal failures the loop reacted to. Several identical failures become one row (Seen), one repair turn runs at a time, a row gets at most two turns and then goes to the Backlog. 'Expected' means the error is the system working as designed.
views.empty: No terminal failures waiting for a repair.

actions.label: Not worth fixing
actions.confirm: Mark this repair as expected? It will not be re-triggered for this signature.
actions.promptHint: Why is this not worth fixing? (recorded)

views.title: Guardrail alerts
views.description: System-level watch on the core reliability metrics across every change window. An alert names the metric, the move, and the changes made in that period — a signal to investigate, not an automatic revert.
views.empty: No guardrail alerts — the core reliability metrics are holding their window.

views.title: Loop settings
views.description: The loop's own knobs, changeable at runtime — the nightly run, the night drain, the Adopt flow and the notify guard all read them live. Saved changes apply immediately, no reload, no restart.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Self-evolve enabled
fields.placeholder: The package ships disabled; the nightly and meta runs no-op until this is on

fields.name: inflight_stale_hours
fields.label: In-flight reclaim (hours)
fields.placeholder: An adopted item in-flight longer than this is reclaimed (1-168)

fields.name: implement_timeout_sec
fields.label: Implement silence budget (sec)
fields.placeholder: An implementation or repair turn must finish within this window (60-7200)

fields.name: drain_cutoff_hour
fields.label: Drain cutoff (hour, server local)
fields.placeholder: The night drain stops starting new items at this hour (0-23)

fields.name: drain_max_per_night
fields.label: Drain max items per night
fields.placeholder: Autonomous backlog items started per night, max (1-12)

fields.name: outcome_measure_days
fields.label: Outcome measurement window (days)
fields.placeholder: A change is judged after this many days (1-14)

fields.name: regression_tolerance
fields.label: Regression tolerance (multiplier)
fields.placeholder: Past baseline x this in the wrong direction counts (1.0-3.0)
